analysis:
The supplied units are BASE-side text of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 1629-2248). The PR changes are documentation only, and the head-side hunks (lines 404-413 and 1053-1073) are visible only in the truncated patch excerpt, so I could not examine them in full. Per the patch excerpt, the changes describe provider memory-load gating: releasing reclaimable free KV segments and MLX's buffer cache before eviction, and parking free 64 MiB paged segments per pool up to min(2 GiB, slot grant/8), outside the grant and ledger charge. The excerpt is cut off at "New segments wrap zero-fil...", so I did not see the zero-fill and clearing semantics. No code, wire protocol, attestation, authorization or key-handling files changed in what I could see.

Security-relevant item for a later pass: the parked free KV segments are reused across requests of the same size class. Whether they are zeroed or cleared before reinstall bears on T-028 (residual inference data in GPU memory) and on cross-request/cross-tenant leakage (A-001). The visible text mentions "zero-fil", which suggests new segments are zero-filled, but reinstalled parked segments may retain prior KV contents until overwritten. This is a documented design statement, not a demonstrated regression. Segments parked outside the grant and ledger charge also raise a memory-accounting and availability question (T-029), but the docs say they are released before loads or evictions.

BASE units 6 and 7 (the MiMo, Flint, invariants and code-map sections) are unchanged context. They have no new attack surface from this PR. The prefix-cache text matches the T-041 posture (encrypted SSD, HMAC names, scoped salt) and nothing in the visible diff alters it. Since the paged-segment hunk is truncated and no code is supplied, I flag needs_deeper_review for the segment reuse and clearing contract.
